Use two standard characterizations.

- For the Möbius clause, use that \(\mu(n)=0\) when \(n\) is not squarefree, while for squarefree \(n\),
  \[
  \mu(n)=(-1)^{\#\{\text{prime divisors of }n\}}\in\{1,-1\}.
  \]
  Thus \(\mu(n)\neq0\) exactly when its value is \(1\) or \(-1\). The case \(n=0\) falls into the zero/non-squarefree branch.

- For the second equivalence, prove both sides independently. The left side is simply `min_le_right`. For the right side, split on `Nat.Prime n` and prove equality of finsets extensionally. Membership in `Nat.primesBelow (n+1)` means that \(p\) is prime and \(p<n+1\); for naturals,
  \[
  p<n+1 \iff p<n \ \lor\ p=n.
  \]
  The new element \(n\) therefore appears precisely when \(n\) is prime, giving the stated `ite`. Since both sides are unconditional truths, each direction of the outer `Iff` may ignore its hypothesis.
